name: aws0-laboon-first
thesis: Lead with the workload, not the transport. A local AWS emulator that cannot run the user's code tests nothing: /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-research-2026-11-19/linkedin-post.txt records a 52/54 API-check result that still failed to load a single Lambda bundle because the shipped embedded JS engine lacked node:http, node:zlib and fetch, and warns that 'a lenient emulator hides bugs. A strict one that cannot run your code tests nothing.' This design therefore makes laboon the preinstalled workload runtime FIRST, and derives every other layer (iroh P2P, CRDT, scheduling, routing, healing, smartops) as a consequence of hosting real processes. laboon (README: /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-research-2026-11-19/_laboon-ref/laboon-main.md, lines 14-35) runs unmodified Linux binaries and OCI images with guest machine code executing natively on the host CPU, intercepting only syscall instructions; there is no VM, no second kernel, no daemon, no Docker socket, and no root. Its tested workload set (lines 161-168) includes PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Redis, Go, Java, Python, Node.js with V8 JIT, .NET and nested podman/Docker. RDS therefore boots real postgres:16 / mysql:8, ElastiCache boots real redis:7 / valkey:8, ECS and Lambda boot the user's real OCI image, Athena boots a real DuckDB SQL engine over real Parquet bytes, and S3 object bytes are real iroh-blobs content. These are not reimplemented subsets: /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/vendor/engine/src/lib.rs lines 37-40 forbids echoing input back, pattern-matching source text and hand-writing a subset evaluator. The existing checkout is a 440-service-crate control plane whose root Cargo.toml is GENERATED and must not be edited, whose README.md line 43 demands at least 100 GB of free disk for a full build, and which has hard documented fidelity gaps (/Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-research-2026-11-19/census.md: 5355 open in-repo issue docs, 7114 stub files, 518 open GitHub issues, 111 CRITICAL). New code lives in a SEPARATE Cargo workspace at /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0-fabric/, plus an optional thin path-dependency seam in at most FIVE per-crate Cargo.toml files, which AGENTS.md explicitly permits. Everything else is substrate: iroh supplies Node discovery/QUIC transport, iroh-docs and iroh-blobs supply replicated desired state and content-addressed persistence, iroh-gossip supplies membership, quic-rpc supplies control RPC, n0-dns-resolver and tokio-rustls-acme supply ordinary DNS and ordinary TLS certificates. All of it is abstracted away: the user runs `aws0 up`, sets one AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, and uses the standard AWS CLI/SDK, psql, redis-cli and curl. No NodeId, EndpointId, Ticket, ALPN, CRDT, region-shard, relay or P2P term ever appears in a modeled response or in the default UX. HONESTY, STATED UP FRONT: this is NOT 1:1 AWS parity and does not claim it. The 440 control-plane crates keep their published fidelity scores and gaps; laboon's own README lines 33-35 says it 'is newer, with a small host surface by design; its daemon and OCI runtime should not be read as claims of production maturity or complete engine compatibility.' Where a workload cannot run, the operation returns the service's modeled error or the scaffold's 501 with a typed Refusal::Unsupported, never a fabricated success. IMPLEMENTATION ORDER is the crate_layout array, which is topologically sorted by depends_on; build_and_witness restates it as phases P0..P9.

crate_layout.responsibility: Pure, total, IO-free algebra. The single vocabulary every other crate imports; no async, no env read, no global/static mutable state. Every effectful function in the system takes an explicit Capability, Clock, Entropy, Net and Store parameter. Refinement types are newtypes whose only constructor validates (RegionId <=32 bytes, ImageDigest is 32 bytes, ResourceId is nonempty), so ill-formed states are unrepresentable.

Zero-trust authorization. ed25519 signing/verifying over (subject, object, action, epoch, expiry, caveats, audience). SigningKey is affine: it is moved into the Signer at boot, is not Clone, and never leaves the process; only public keys, signatures and opaque Capability values cross a boundary. No ambient identity, no process-global principal, no credentials in any AST or log. Verified at ingress, at CRDT write, at sandbox spawn, at relay connect and at blob download.

THE LABOON-FIRST CORE. Preinstall, checksum/signature verification, pinned OCI image catalog, sandbox supervision, CLI argv construction, guest-side bridging, health probes and typed refusals. Drives the prebuilt `laboon` binary as a managed child with an explicit argv (never a shell), using -image/-root/-entrypoint/-platform/-mem/-net/-no-net/-mount HOST:GUEST/-env KEY=VALUE/-allow-domains/-allow-cidrs/-allow-ports/-reject-rwx flags from cmd/laboon/main.go. Contains no iroh and no aws0 dependency, so it can be witnessed standalone on one node.

The ONLY crate the existing aws0 checkout may depend on. Deliberately tiny (a Unix-domain-socket dialer plus a length-prefixed frame relay), zero iroh/laboon/rustls dependencies, so adding it to five per-crate Cargo.toml files does not drag the fabric into the 100 GB workspace build. It implements the NativeHandler/HttpHandler backend contract described in vendor/engine/src/lib.rs lines 20-35 by relaying raw protocol bytes to the aws0d daemon, while the core still owns the socket, TLS and bind interface. A service handler never binds a socket, chooses a port or configures TLS itself.

Replicated desired state. Bindings to iroh-docs 0.101.0 (DocsApi::spawn, Doc, Doc::set_bytes, Doc::set_hash, Doc::get_many, NamespaceId, AuthorId, Author, DocTicket, Replica, Entry, AuthorHeads) and to iroh-blobs 0.105.0 (Hash, HashAndFormat, HashSeq, Blobs, Downloader, BlobTicket). Our own CRDTs are pure join-semilattice morphisms stored as content-addressed heads; history is an append-only HashSeq DAG, so knowledge is monotone. One NamespaceId per (account, region, service) is the constructive proof that state sets are disjoint.

The hidden substrate. iroh 1.5.0 Endpoint/Router, ALPN-registered ProtocolHandlers, quic-rpc 0.20.0 control RPC, iroh-gossip 0.103.0 membership broadcast, n0-dns-resolver 0.1.1 discovery records, tokio-rustls-acme 0.10.0 certificate issuance. IMPORTANT ACCURACY NOTE: iroh 1.5.0 renamed NodeId->EndpointId and NodeAddr->EndpointAddr (verified in iroh-base/src/endpoint_addr.rs); any design citing NodeAddr is stale. iroh-docs' own internal RPC is irpc/noq, not quic-rpc; we use quic-rpc only for our own control service and do not claim a shared transport.

Persistence across restarts. Desired state on disk via the iroh-docs replica, immutable artifacts/volumes/snapshots via iroh-blobs (BlobTicket::new(EndpointAddr, Hash, BlobFormat)), a node-local small KV (redb, or the vendored iroh-smol-kv source kept under vendor-ref/ as a reference, never claimed as a crates.io dependency) for membership/lease/metric caches. Restore is a pure fold over the event log followed by reattachment of volume tickets and re-spawn of sandboxes with the same ResourceId and Epoch.

Placement and horizontal scaling with no global lock. Consistent-hash ring over (RegionId, ServiceId, ResourceId) with virtual nodes; each node owns a disjoint shard, admission is local, conflicting placements resolve by CRDT join on monotone Epoch. Scaling is driven by measured p99 and queue depth against a P99Budget; there are NO artificial job, credit or count caps - only measured PhysicsVector bounds (CPU, RAM, disk, file descriptors).

Membership, failure detection and self-healing. SWIM-style membership over iroh-gossip with Phi-accrual suspicion, Byzantine-safe affine typestate transitions Joining->Alive->Suspect->Dead->Tombstone that require a signed, epoch-monotone Proof and forbid resurrection. Reconciler is a total loop over (reduce(DesiredState), probe(ObservedState), diff, apply(idempotent)).

User-facing ingress and endpoint registry. One ordinary HTTPS hostname per region, resolved with n0-dns-resolver SVCB/HTTPS/SRV/TXT records to the nearest healthy node; certificate from tokio-rustls-acme (AcmeConfig::state, ResolvesServerCertAcme) or an auto-installed local CA when offline. SigV4 headers are forwarded verbatim - never forged, stripped or re-signed - so the control plane remains the sole signature verifier (AGENTS.md line 87). Presigned URLs and queue URLs are NEVER rewritten (AGENTS.md lines 75-85). Circuit breaking honors a measured p99 budget.

Adapter to the untouched 440-crate checkout. Launches the checksum-verified prebuilt aws-emulator-router binary per node with explicit --fabric-socket/--fabric-token argv capability and EMULATOR_DATA_PORT / EMULATOR_BIND_ADDRESS / EMULATOR_LISTENER_PORT_RANGE. Primary seam (Mode B): five per-crate Cargo.toml files gain a path dependency on fabric-bridge and five ops/*.rs handlers relay their native protocol through it; endpoint fields STILL come from the core-owned listener.authority()/listener.url() (vendor/engine/src/lib.rs lines 28-35). Fallback seam (Mode A) for untouched services: a typed, protocol-aware EndpointProjection in the ingress replaces ONLY the endpoint address members of a modeled output for resources that have a real workload; presigned URLs and ctx.endpoint()-derived URLs are never touched. Root Cargo.toml, core/router/src/lib.rs, core/router/src/main.rs and vendor/ are never edited. HONEST LIMIT: the control plane's private InMemoryEngine state is per-process and is NOT transparently CRDT-replicated; HA is N replicas plus a per-resource fenced lease plus the authoritative desired-state doc.

The automated 'protocol'-defined smartops layer. A small total DSL: a Protocol is a bounded Plan of Steps, each with pre/post predicates, one Effect and one compensating Effect. Runner::run is a pure fold producing an Outcome; the Interpreter is the only place IO happens. IdempotencyKey = BLAKE3(resource_id || step.name || epoch). Every exception is mapped to Outcome::Refused(Refusal) or Outcome::Degraded(Reason) - total, no partiality, no unhandled branch, no phantom variant, no placeholder comment. Protocol documents are deny_unknown_fields TOML under protocols/ with a schema version.

Node daemon binary (src/main.rs) and user CLI (src/bin/aws0.rs). `aws0 up` runs the boot Protocol, prints one endpoint and writes AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_CA_BUNDLE and credentials for the user's shell; `aws0 status`, `aws0 logs`, `aws0 nodes` report in plain language. Boot reads env ONCE into BootConfig, then passes capabilities explicitly: no ambient state at any call site.

Off-repo witness harness, deliberately independent of the implementation. Drives real psql, redis-cli, duckdb, node and AWS CLI against the fabric; runs the five strictness checks from linkedin-post.txt; runs chaos (kill node, partition, restart, max load) and asserts convergence, data integrity and p99 bounds; greps authored sources for TODO/FIXME/ellipsis markers, unwrap, panic, todo! and unsafe and fails on any hit.

DESIGN. (1) One NamespaceId per (AccountId, RegionId, ServiceId), computed as BLAKE3 of the canonical byte encoding of that triple. Namespaces are the disjoint state sets S_i: iroh-docs entries are scoped by NamespaceId, therefore S_i intersect S_j is empty by construction for distinct triples. (2) One AuthorId per node, derived from that node's iroh EndpointId; a node writes ONLY with its own Author. This is the disjoint response/write set R_i: tags are (EndpointId, epoch, counter), so no two nodes can emit the same tag and R_i intersect R_j is empty. (3) Layer pure CRDTs OVER the doc, never raw last-write-wins: ORSet<T> for replica membership and endpoint records (add-tag/remove-tag with unique tags), LwwRegister<T> for a resource's current spec with a total (Lamport, EndpointId) order, GCounter/PNCounter for observed load and replica count, FencedLease for single-writer ownership, Tombstone for deletion. Each exposes merge: (S,S)->S that is associative, commutative and idempotent, verified by property tests in fabric-crdt. (4) Monotone knowledge Gamma_t superset Gamma_{t-1}: every Event is an immutable iroh-blobs object; heads form an append-only HashSeq DAG. Doc::set_hash points the key at the current head Hash. Nothing is ever deleted from the DAG; compaction replaces a prefix P with Snapshot(P) only when a CompactionProof establishes join(Snapshot(P), X) == join(P, X) for all X. Compaction is therefore a semantics-preserving morphism, not truncation. (5) Delta is minimal: a mutating operation appends exactly one Event and one head pointer; no full-state broadcast. iroh-blobs deduplicates identical artifacts by Hash, so N nodes holding the same image or volume snapshot store one logical object. (6) Convergence: iroh-docs gossip/sync reconciles AuthorHeads; our reducer is a join-semilattice homomorphism, so any two replicas that have observed the same set of Events compute the same DocState. Partition heals by union of Event sets, never by rollback. (7) CAP honesty: the desired-state doc is AP (always writable locally, converges on heal), which is correct for resource metadata. Single-writer leases are CP inside a region: Lease{resource_id, epoch, holder, quorum} requires a majority of in-region replicas to acknowledge the epoch before any sandbox may be spawned, and every spawn carries the epoch as a fence that the supervisor re-verifies. Cross-region is AP; we do NOT claim cross-region linearizability. consensus_and_cap states this again. (8) iroh-dag-sync and iroh-smol-kv are repository tools in the iroh monorepo, NOT published crates in the verified index; their sources are vendored read-only under aws0-fabric/vendor-ref/ for the blob-DAG sync protocol and the small-KV reference. They are never declared as Cargo dependencies. (9) No secrets in the AST: a DocTicket or BlobTicket is a public capability value carrying an EndpointAddr/EndpointId and a Hash; author private keys live only in the affine SigningKey typestate.
scheduling: Scheduler::place(ResourceId, WorkloadSpec, Ring, ResourceVector, &Capability) -> ScheduleDecision is a total, deterministic, IO-free function except for the explicit Effect that reads measured node load. (1) Ownership by consistent hashing: Ring maps H(RegionId || ServiceId || ResourceId) to VirtualNode -> EndpointId. Because the hash is a pure function, every node independently computes the same owner; there is no coordinator, no leader election, no global lock, and therefore no serialization point whose contention grows with n. (2) Admission is local: the owning node checks its own measured ResourceVector (cpu_millis, mem_bytes, disk_bytes, fds) against WorkloadSpec. If it cannot admit, it returns ScheduleDecision::Delegate(next candidate on the ring) with a signed Proof; the caller retries against a disjoint candidate. (3) Conflicts: two nodes racing on the same ResourceId produce two Placement events; FencedLease::merge takes the max Epoch (monotone join), the loser's spawns are refused by the epoch fence at SandboxSupervisor, and the loser's Effect is a no-op. Thus contention is confined to one resource's lease, and as n grows the number of resources per node shard falls, so per-node contention tends to 0. (4) Idempotence: Placement is keyed by (ResourceId, Epoch) in an ORSet; place(place(x)) == place(x). Spawn is keyed by the same pair in the SandboxHandle registry, guarded by the node's lease, so a replayed Event never creates a second postgres process. (5) Scaling: ScalePolicy{metric, P99Budget, cooldown}; Metrics come from gossiped Heartbeats (not guesses). A ScaleDecision changes only a PNCounter of desired replicas; the reconciler realizes it by place/spawn/retire. Scale-up triggers when measured p99 exceeds the budget; scale-down when p99 is comfortably below it and load is low. Bounds are physics-only - measured CPU, RAM, disk and FD availability on the node - with NO artificial job count, credit, spend or quota caps. (6) Multi-region: RegionId is part of every key (the RDS state in /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/services/service-com-amazonaws-rds-amazonrdsv19/src/state.rs already keys every map by (region, identifier), so one identifier legitimately names a different instance per region). The ring is per region; a region's placements never cross into another region's namespace. (7) Multi-node: any node may receive a request; RouteKey hashes to the owner, and the ingress forwards over iroh with ALPN /aws0/relay/1. The user never learns which node owns what. (8) Bounding: every placement and spawn is wrapped in tokio::time::timeout, exactly as /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-2026-11-19/aws0/vendor/engine/src/lib.rs lines 53-57 requires ('Bound it'), and each sandbox carries an explicit WithMaxMemory-equivalent -mem and an OutputCap; exceeding a bound is a typed Refusal, not a silent truncation.

On restart, RestartPlan replays the doc, reattaches the volume ticket locally or downloads it via BlobTicket, and re-spawns the sandbox with the same ResourceId and a NEW epoch (epochs are monotone, never reused). Because reduce is a join-semilattice homomorphism, replaying in any order yields the same state; no WAL replay ordering hazard. A network partition can leave two control-plane replicas divergent; on heal the desired-state doc is authoritative and the loser is rebuilt by replay. This is stated, not hidden. self_healing: Membership: iroh-gossip 0.103.0 (verified /Users/dylanwong/projects/aws0-research-2026-11-19/_work/iroh-gossip-0.103.0-extracted/iroh-gossip-0.103.0/src/net.rs line 72 Gossip, line 335 subscribe_with_opts, line 366 subscribe_and_join, line 386 subscribe; api.rs line 37 GossipSender, line 87 broadcast(Bytes), line 138 GossipTopic, line 173 broadcast(Bytes), line 216 GossipReceiver). Heartbeats carry EndpointId, Epoch, RegionId, ResourceVector and a DocState head Hash; Phi-accrual suspicion replaces a fixed timeout, so a slow node is not killed by an arbitrary clock value. Typestate (affine, Byzantine): Joining -> Alive -> Suspect -> Dead -> Tombstone. Each transition consumes a signed, epoch-monotone Proof and produces a new MemberView; there is NO Dead -> Alive edge, so a resurrected old node cannot resurrect a stale lease. A node that rejoins does so with a fresh EndpointId and a fresh AuthorId, which preserves R_i disjointness. Reconciler: a total loop, loop { desired = reduce(DocState); observed = probe(Sandboxes, Members); diff = desired \ observed; apply_idempotent(diff); }. probe is bounded by tokio::time::timeout; a probe failure becomes ObservedState::Unknown for that node, never a guessed 'healthy'. apply only ever calls place/spawn/retire/attach, all keyed by (ResourceId, Epoch), so applying the same diff twice is a no-op (f o f == f). Healing cases, all witnessed: (a) sandbox crash -> restart from the same volume ticket with a new epoch; (b) node loss -> Phi confirms Dead, quorum grants a new fenced lease, ring delegates the placement to the next candidate, artifacts are fetched via BlobTicket, volume reattached; (c) network partition -> AP desired-state replicas continue locally, CP leases refuse spawns without quorum, on heal the Event sets union and the reducer converges; (d) corrupted blob -> Hash mismatch is a StoreRefusal, the artifact is re-fetched from another replica; (e) stuck/slow workload -> p99 budget opens the CircuitBreaker and the workload is drained and replaced, never a hang. Graceful degradation is p99-bounded: on any refusal the API returns the service's modeled error or Outcome::Degraded(Reason) with an explicit retry hint; it never returns a fabricated success and never spins. No artificial caps: heal retries are bounded by measured physics (disk, CPU, p99), not by a credit or job-count gate.

consensus_and_cap: There is NO cluster-wide consensus log and NO Kubernetes. Consensus is scoped to one resource at a time. FencedLease{resource_id, epoch, holder: EndpointIdRef, quorum: usize} is granted only when a majority of in-region replicas acknowledge the epoch; the epoch is a monotone fence carried into every spawn, every volume attach and every EndpointPublisher write, and the supervisor re-verifies it before touching a sandbox. A stale holder cannot act. This is CP, linearizable per resource within one region, and it is the ONLY place a quorum is required. Desired-state metadata (specs, placements, endpoints, membership, protocol keys) is AP: it is an iroh-docs CRDT that remains writable on both sides of a partition and converges by lattice join on heal. Cross-region replication is AP; we explicitly do NOT claim cross-region linearizability, global transactions, or a single serializable history. Partition behavior is declared per ServiceClass: AP for metadata and read-mostly services; CP for single-writer data-plane resources (a database, a cache, a volume) where two writers would corrupt state. On a CP partition the minority side returns Outcome::Degraded(Partition) or the service's modeled error; it never spawns a second writer.
